speaker: elowen
text: Rise, Knight of the Dawn.

speaker: elowen
text: Take it! Follow me down â I'll leave you a trail!

speaker: elowen
text: To Emberhollow â and to whoever finally finishes Marga's pie!

speaker: elowen
text: Note 6: "Mushrooms that scream. I am not making this up. Kill the little ones first."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 8: "Brakk carries a dwarf-made hammer far too fine for him. Brambur will know it."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 3: "Water to my knees. Sister Vey sings to the old lizard. It is very bad singing."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 10: "His staff is the anchor. Break it and I am free. I will be ready. â Your friend, E."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 1: "If you are reading this, you followed. Good. They tied my hands but not my pencil. â E."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 2: "The spider-rider is called Skarn. He talks to his mount. It does not answer. Neither do I."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 5: "The crystals hum when the basilisk looks at them. Mirrors, perhaps? Bring something shiny."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 4: "Malthrax says there are five seals and one breaks with every moonrise. Hurry. But eat something."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 7: "Ashforge. They chain smiths to the anvils. The chimera wears a collar â Brakk is afraid of it."

speaker: elowen
text: Note 9: "I can see the vault. Something very large is sleeping under the floor. Malthrax keeps saying 'Gorvax'."

speaker: malthrax
text: Princess. You will make a lovely key.

speaker: malthrax
text: Five moons, Emberhollow. Then you kneel before Blackspire.

speaker: narrator
text: The ground shakes. Bones of enormous beasts form an archway here, and the hot, rotten wind blowing through it is breath.

speaker: narrator
text: The forge-hall opens up around an anvil the size of a wagon, glowing white-hot. Heavy footsteps ring out from beyond the smoke.

speaker: narrator
text: The cave drops into a drowned amphitheatre, water black and mirror-still. Ripples spread from the centre, where nothing should be.

speaker: narrator
text: Crystals here grow in a perfect ring around a pedestal of black glass. Your reflections in them stop moving when you do. Then one of them smiles.

speaker: narrator
text: The tunnel widens into a nest of chewed bones, gnawed armour and stolen cutlery, piled into a lopsided throne. Something big stirs on top of it and sniffs the air.

speaker: wren
text: Mind the basilisk, dear.

speaker: osric
text: The Temple stands with you.

speaker: dobbin
text: The forges are lit for you.

speaker: marga
text: Room's ready whenever you are.

speaker: tamsin
text: Blow it hard. Wake the valley.

speaker: rowan
text: The town's behind you. Bring her home.

speaker: marga
text: Nobody finishes my pie. That's the tradition.

speaker: rowan
text: All four, alive! Here's 75 gold. They'll walk the Warrens with you from now on.

speaker: osric
text: Her relics! The Temple owes you a life â one Raise Dead, free. And take these.

speaker: rowan
text: One more thing, Knight. The Sovereign's staff... we never found it among the rubble.

speaker: wren
text: Perfect caps! Three Potions of Stone-to-Flesh. Drink one if you start feeling... gravelly.

speaker: dobbin
text: My brothers are home. This blade took all six of us to forge. +2, and it sings when it cuts.

speaker: marga
text: Quiet as a tomb down there now. Rooms are free for you, love. Forever. Don't tell the others.

speaker: dobbin
text: They took my brother smiths to the Ashforge in chains. Free them and I'll forge you the finest blade in Emberhollow.

speaker: marga
text: Something's digging into my cellar from below. Scratching all night. Collapse that tunnel and you'll never pay for a room again.

speaker: wren
text: Glowcaps! The Glimmerdeep is full of them. Three, and I can brew you something for basilisk trouble. Stone-to-flesh, dear. Very fashionable.

speaker: rowan
text: Four of my guards chased the cultists into the Rat-Warrens and never came back. Bring them home and I'll see you paid â and they'll fight at your side.

speaker: osric
text: The princess carried a satchel of relics from this temple. If it survived, it fell in the Drowned Grotto. Bring it back and the Temple will owe you a life.

speaker: rowan
text: You. You fought like the Dawn's own knight. Take this writ â it gives you the Crown's authority below. Bring her back. I'll have work for you in town, too.

speaker: tamsin
text: When I was a girl, the Warden kept a horn that woke the whole valley. It's down in the vault still. Sound it when the big lizard wakes â trust an old woman.

speaker: narrator
text: Cold water closes over your boots, and the splash rolls away through vaulted caves. Pale fungus glows above black pools far deeper than they look. The air tastes of salt and rust. Something large shifts beneath the Drowned Grotto, then goes still.

speaker: narrator
text: The Glimmerdeep opens like the inside of a geode, its crystals humming one endless note. A hundred reflections march beside you, each a heartbeat out of step. The air smells of flint and ozone. Deeper in stand statues frozen in surprise. Nobody carved them.

speaker: narrator
text: Wet steps lead down into low, dripping tunnels that reek of damp straw and old cheese. Tiny claws scritch in every crack. Your torch catches dozens of red eyes that blink out the moment you look. Somewhere ahead a soup-tin bell tinkles once: the Rat-Warrens are awake.

speaker: narrator
text: Silence falls like a lid. Colossal pillars carved with roaring lizards rise into darkness above claw-scored floors. The air smells of warm scales and old blood, and trembles with slow, heavy breathing. Elowen's light lies somewhere beyond. So does the thing that guards it.

speaker: narrator
text: Heat slaps your face. Slag crawls glowing through dwarf-cut channels, and hammers ring from forges that should be cold. Ash sifts down, bitter with sulphur, gritty between your teeth. Every shadow flickers, and some flicker back. Whatever feeds the Ashforge is still hungry.

speaker: narrator
text: Far below, in the dark of the empty vault, a sixth seal nobody knew about begins to glow.

speaker: narrator
text: Gorvax the Tyrant crashes down, and the Blackspire shudders. One by one its violet lights go dark.

speaker: narrator
text: The fire goes out. Elowen is gone. The floor of the cellar has cracked open onto a stair leading down.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadow-hands seize Elowen. As she is dragged into the fire, she wrenches her signet ring free and throws it to you.

speaker: narrator
text: As the last cultist falls, the hearth fire turns violet. A tall shadow steps out of it, wearing a crown of black iron.

speaker: narrator
text: Emberhollow, harvest night. The Boar & Spoon is packed to the rafters, and Princess Elowen herself is pouring the cider.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the candles gutter out, all at once. Robed figures pour through the cellar door, with rats and wolf-spiders at their heels.

speaker: narrator
text: Back in Emberhollow, in the Boar & Spoon, which is still missing a few spoons, Elowen draws Dawnfang and lays it on your shoulder.

speaker: narrator
text: You raise the Warden's Warhorn and blow. The note rolls up through five floors of stone, and far above, Emberhollow's bells answer.

speaker: vexrath
text: Victory, duly notarised.

speaker: brambur
text: ll take first watch. I won

speaker: grumsh
text: We won. And yetâ¦ did we?

speaker: brambur
text: m terribly sorry about what

speaker: grumsh
text: I grow stronger. My sorrow grows with me.

speaker: vexrath
text: I will catch up on my backlog of blessings.

speaker: grumsh
text: Ah. Violence. The only song I was ever good at.

speaker: grumsh
text: I will keep watch. Sleep is for the untroubled.

speaker: vexrath
text: Promotion granted! I shall need a bigger stamp.

speaker: grumsh
text: Victory. I shall compose something unbearably moving.

speaker: grumsh
text: Grumsh joins. Grumsh has packed his lute and his sorrow.

speaker: vexrath
text: Hostile encounter logged. Form 7-B: Smiting, commencing.

speaker: vexrath
text: Have you filed a permit to attack us? No? Most irregular.

speaker: grumsh
text: Another battle. Another verse for my endless ballad of woe.

speaker: vexrath
text: I have filed my joining papers in triplicate. Let us begin.

speaker: vexrath
text: Rest period approved: eight hours, minus one hour of filing.

speaker: grumsh
text: Let me play you to sleep. It is a lament. They are all laments.

speaker: vexrath
text: Encounter closed. Outcome: favourable. Please rate your smiting experience.

speaker: grumsh
text: Very well. I shall follow you into the dark. It is where I keep my feelings anyway.

speaker: vexrath
text: Application approved. Vexrath Quillscale, paladin, reporting. Please initial here, here and here.

speaker: liora
text: Liora Wardenfall, Warden's Watch. My father went down into the Blackspire twenty years ago. I'm done waiting at the door. Mind if I join you?

speaker: liora
text: I shoot, I track, and I'm told I'm very good company. Mostly by myself, but still.

speaker: liora
text: Do you mind if I sit? The fire is better company than the dark.

speaker: liora
text: This clasp was my father's. Aldous Wardenfall, last Warden of the Watch. He took the horn and went down to reseal the vault. I was nine.

speaker: liora
text: Every floor, I find a little of him. Tally marks. A boot. I haven't told anyone I talk to the marks.

speaker: liora
text: ...Thank you. Most people want me to cheer up.

speaker: liora
text: You're very easy to talk to. Annoyingly easy.

speaker: liora
text: Ha! He would have loved you. Terrible taste, my father.

speaker: liora
text: Thank you. I needed to laugh more than I knew.

speaker: liora
text: Don't promise what the dark might not give back.

speaker: liora
text: ...But I'll hold you to it. Gently. With a bow.

speaker: liora
text: You're soaked through. So am I. Don't look; I'm not at my best when I'm dripping.

speaker: liora
text: I found his lantern, hung above the tide line. Still tended. He was still being careful.

speaker: liora
text: I find that comforting and unbearable, both.

speaker: liora
text: A cloak. A hero's cloak. You smell like campfire and rat.

speaker: liora
text: Keep smelling exactly like that. It's very warm, thank you.

speaker: liora
text: You're good at this. The quiet. Don't let anyone talk you out of it.

speaker: liora
text: Oh, you are going to pay for that. Slowly. In small, annoying ways.

speaker: liora
text: Every crystal down here shows me what I want. Then takes it back.

speaker: liora
text: One of those reflections smiled at me with his face.

speaker: liora
text: I know it's only the glass. I know. It still lands.

speaker: liora
text: Your hand's warm. ...Okay. I can look now.

speaker: liora
text: Don't let go yet. Not until the crystals stop.

speaker: liora
text: That's smooth. Ridiculous. Do it again later.

speaker: liora
text: I may have blushed. It was the crystals. Obviously.

speaker: liora
text: Practical. Fair. Thank you for not letting me spiral.

speaker: liora
text: Ember light suits you. I mean that as a compliment. Mostly.

speaker: liora
text: Can I ask something? Is there someone waiting for you up top? A family? A person you write to?

speaker: liora
text: Careful. I'm very good at keeping the things I find.

speaker: liora
text: That might be the nicest thing anyone has said to me in the dark.

speaker: liora
text: I'll take it. I'll keep it.

speaker: liora
text: Mm. Deflecting. I see you. I'll let you off. This once.

speaker: liora
text: Tomorrow this ends, one way or the other. I found his boots at the stair. Only the boots.

speaker: liora
text: Whatever the vault holds, I'd like to have asked something first, so I don't wonder for another twenty years.

speaker: liora
text: Yes. Obviously yes.

speaker: liora
text: Beside me. I can do beside.

speaker: liora
text: Deal. I'll hold the sun up myself if I have to.

speaker: liora
text: He kept something burning down here for twenty years. Whatever that last light is, I will be the one to find it.

speaker: liora
text: I'm staying in Emberhollow. If the Knight will have me.

speaker: liora
text: I'll keep the lantern lit in my window. And maybe, if you ask nicely, keep your fire company too.

speaker: liora
text: Thank you for walking me to him. Whatever comes next, I'm glad you were beside me.

speaker: liora
text: Five-bar tally marks scratched low on the wall. That's the Watch's count. Dad was here.

speaker: liora
text: Twenty-nine days of marks. Then they stop. I want to know why.

speaker: liora
text: A lantern hangs above the tide line, its wick still fresh. Someone has tended it.

speaker: liora
text: Someone. Or something kind. I'd settle for either.

speaker: liora
text: A journal page, tucked in a crystal seam: "The seals hold only if the sixth is kept."

speaker: liora
text: Sixth? There are five. Isn't that the whole point?

speaker: liora
text: A Watch sword, laid in the cooling trough. His grip-wrap. Not broken. Left.

speaker: liora
text: Like he put it down on purpose. Like he had somewhere to be.

speaker: liora
text: Dad's boots, at the foot of the stair. Side by side. Neat, like him.

speaker: liora
text: I think he walked the rest of the way barefoot. That's exactly like him.

speaker: liora
text: Quiet in here. Quiet that's been practising.

speaker: liora
text: Fresh tracks near the wall. Keep your eyes up.

speaker: liora
text: Look at the floor dust. Someone passed here recently. Or something wearing boots.

speaker: liora
text: Dad always said to check every chest twice. I'll hold your torch.

speaker: liora
text: A nice find. Keep what helps, leave what haunts you.

speaker: liora
text: A hidden door. Dad would have been so smug. Let's be smug for him.

speaker: liora
text: I knew that wall was wrong. I just wanted you to feel clever.

speaker: liora
text: That one's dangerous. We go slow, we go together.

speaker: liora
text: Stay close. It watches the corridor, but it hasn't seen the bow yet.

speaker: liora
text: Smell that? Bread and woodsmoke. It's nice to be reminded what we're fighting for.

speaker: liora
text: I'll light the lantern in my window, just in case. Old habit.

speaker: liora
text: Arrows nocked. Let us make this quick.

speaker: liora
text: Stay behind me. Or in front. Honestly, I'll shoot around you.

speaker: liora
text: Right. Time to earn the sun on my clasp.

speaker: liora
text: One less thing in the dark.

speaker: liora
text: Clean shot. Don't tell the others I'm pleased.

speaker: liora
text: Straight through the eye. I do love a bright day.

speaker: liora
text: Oh, that felt good.

speaker: liora
text: Ow. Rude.

speaker: liora
text: Fair. I'd have done the same.

speaker: liora
text: I'm fine. I'm... mostly fine.

speaker: liora
text: Somebody tell the floor to stop hitting me.

speaker: liora
text: Now THAT was worth the climb.

speaker: liora
text: Shiny. Dad always said to check every chest twice.

speaker: liora
text: Deeper. He went this way. I can feel it.

speaker: liora
text: One more stair. One more step closer.

speaker: liora
text: I'll take first watch. I don't sleep much down here anyway.

speaker: liora
text: Come sit by the fire. It's the one warm thing in this whole place.

speaker: liora
text: I SAW that. I was just choosing to be brave about it.

speaker: liora
text: Dad's lessons: step light, curse softly.

speaker: liora
text: Well fought, all of you. Truly.

speaker: liora
text: Another one down. I could get used to this.

speaker: liora
text: Stronger, and still not close enough to him. But closer.

speaker: liora
text: A hidden door. Dad loved those. He would be so smug.

speaker: liora
text: I know this kind of silence. Someone was here recently, or never left.

speaker: liora
text: Mind the shadows. And the floor. And, well, everything.

speaker: liora
text: The Watch taught me to read tracks. Dad taught me to read people. Only one of those is any use in a dungeon.

speaker: liora
text: I keep a lantern lit for him back home. Marga thinks it's for the inn. I let her.

speaker: liora
text: Half-elf means two families that never quite fit me. So I made a third out of whoever shows up. Hello.

speaker: liora
text: Do you ever notice how the rats are polite? They only bite when you stop looking.

speaker: liora
text: If I ever sing, it's the wind. Agreed? Good.

speaker: brambur
text: I wrote Mum a letter before we left. "Dear Mum, I'm in a cave. Love, Brambur."

speaker: brambur
text: I didn't send it. She'd only worry. She'd also send soup.

speaker: brambur
text: This water reminds me of the font where Mother Pellwen blessed me. It was this cold.

speaker: brambur
text: I cried. She said that's how you know it took.

speaker: brambur
text: I said a prayer for the rats. And the mirrors. Is that strange?

speaker: brambur
text: Mother Pellwen says every creature deserves one prayer. I save the spares for us.

speaker: brambur
text: That hammer of Mum's. It'll be somewhere near here, won't it? The Ashforge.

speaker: brambur
text: I won't hit anyone with it. Probably. Maybe once.

speaker: brambur
text: If we don't come back, tell Mum I was brave. Lie if you must.

speaker: brambur
text: Actually, tell her I apologised to the dragon. That'll make her laugh.

speaker: brambur
text: Nice room. Is it safe? It never is. Lovely.

speaker: brambur
text: I'll just say hello to the walls, so they know we're friendly.

speaker: brambur
text: Is it me, or is this room judging us? Sorry, room.

speaker: brambur
text: I'll write a thank-you note to whoever left this. Posthumously.

speaker: brambur
text: Is it wrong that I'm a little excited? Don't tell Mother Pellwen.

speaker: brambur
text: A secret! I do hope nobody lived in there. Sorry if they did.

speaker: brambur
text: Hidden doors are just doors that are shy. Hello, shy door.

speaker: brambur
text: Oh no. That one is bigger than the others. Sorry. I'll pray quietly.

speaker: brambur
text: We could... not? We could very much not.

speaker: brambur
text: Home! Sort of. Nobody here wants to eat us, which is lovely.

speaker: brambur
text: Fresh air, no scratching, and Marga's pie. Heaven.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick has been informed he is "a bit much." Fizzwick has chosen to be flattered.

speaker: fizzwick
text: ...Fizzwick is flattered. Mostly.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick's thesis was laughed at by the Academy. It was correct. Fizzwick has the scorch marks to prove it.

speaker: fizzwick
text: It was about fire. Their roof, specifically.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick sees himself in these crystals. Brilliant, faceted, and slightly cracked.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick will deny having said that.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick admits the forge is magnificent. Fizzwick does not admit he is sweating.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick is merely... glistening.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Should Fizzwick fall here, he asks that his footnote be larger than the others.

speaker: fizzwick
text: And that someone read it aloud. With feeling.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick approves of the proportions. They are almost as grand as Fizzwick.

speaker: fizzwick
text: The acoustics are splendid. Fizzwick shall test them by being brilliant.

speaker: fizzwick
text: A chamber! Fizzwick shall make a note, and then a bigger note about himself.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick has appraised it. Verdict: Fizzwick's, with minor concessions.

speaker: fizzwick
text: A fine acquisition. Fizzwick will mention it in his memoirs, chapter eleven.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick suspected a hidden passage all along. He was merely waiting for a witness.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Observe: a concealed door. Fizzwick has discovered it with his eyes. Mostly.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick has identified a significant threat. Fizzwick will be standing behind someone.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Statistically, this is where Fizzwick suggests a strategic retreat. Statistically.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Emberhollow! Where Fizzwick's genius is, regrettably, underappreciated.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick shall now bathe in adoration. Or at least a warm bath.

speaker: pip
text: Fun fact: I stole my first spoon at six. My mum wept with pride.

speaker: pip
text: Then she made me give it back. Then I stole it again.

speaker: pip
text: Spoon count: zero. But I found a very good fork. It's a start.

speaker: pip
text: A fork is just a spoon with ambition.

speaker: pip
text: I grew up with eleven cousins and one spoon. You learn to be quick.

speaker: pip
text: I still sleep with it under my pillow. Don't tell the others.

speaker: pip
text: The Spoon-Keepers say a hero's measure is what they leave on the table.

speaker: pip
text: I always leave a spoon. Mostly mine.

speaker: pip
text: If I find that armory, I'll share it. A little. We'll discuss terms.

speaker: pip
text: I'd share all of it, actually. Don't repeat that.

speaker: pip
text: Ooh, a room with no cutlery. Disappointing, but gorgeous.

speaker: pip
text: Anyone else feel watched? No? Just me? I'll check the corners.

speaker: pip
text: Nice room. Good bones. Bad spoons.

speaker: pip
text: Mine, mine, mine. I mean, ours! Ours, ours, mine.

speaker: pip
text: That's a fine find. I'd say it's spoon-adjacent.

speaker: pip
text: Hidden doors are just treasure with manners.

speaker: pip
text: Ha! Called it. I called it in my head. Loudly.

speaker: pip
text: Big one. Nope. Nope nope. I'll be the one holding the door.

speaker: pip
text: Remember: when it chases us, I run fastest. You're welcome.

speaker: pip
text: Smell that? Bread, smoke and other people's spoons. Home.

speaker: pip
text: Town! I'll just... browse. Innocently. Everything.

speaker: grumsh
text: Verse one: "Oh rat, oh rat, you gnawed my boot."

speaker: grumsh
text: It gets better. It does not get shorter.

speaker: grumsh
text: I failed my bardic audition. They said my dirges were "too much." The audience wept.

speaker: grumsh
text: Which was the point, no?

speaker: grumsh
text: A crystal sings one note forever. I envy that. I can't hold a note longer than my temper.

speaker: grumsh
text: Fine. Longer than that. Barely.

speaker: grumsh
text: Verse four is a battle verse. I'm not sure I'm brave enough to write it.

speaker: grumsh
text: I shall be brave. After one more mope.

speaker: grumsh
text: I'll finish the ballad tonight. Whatever happens tomorrow, it has an ending.

speaker: grumsh
text: Even if the ending is: Grumsh hit it very hard.

speaker: grumsh
text: Another hall for the dead to echo in.

speaker: grumsh
text: I hear a verse in this room. A sad one.

speaker: grumsh
text: Quiet halls make loud poets. Please excuse me.

speaker: grumsh
text: Gold for a dirge. Fair trade.

speaker: grumsh
text: Shiny things, brief joy. Write that down.

speaker: grumsh
text: A secret: the oldest rhyme there is. Behind every wall, another wall.

speaker: grumsh
text: Hidden, but not forgotten. Like most of my poetry.

speaker: grumsh
text: The big one. Good. A hero's song needs a worthy verse.

speaker: grumsh
text: I shall hum it a dirge before it falls. Out of respect.

speaker: grumsh
text: A town. People. I'll hum quietly so they don't flee.

speaker: grumsh
text: Warm ale and loud laughter. The only verse I can't write.

speaker: zizzy
text: Confession: I lost my eyebrows at a wedding. Not mine. I was a guest.

speaker: zizzy
text: There was cake. The cake was fine.

speaker: zizzy
text: Water is fire's rival. I respect that. I'll still try to boil it.

speaker: zizzy
text: Gently. For science.

speaker: zizzy
text: These crystals focus light! Which means they can focus FIRE!

speaker: zizzy
text: I know because of the eyebrows.

speaker: zizzy
text: Home! Not home, but this is the first place that smells like my kitchen!

speaker: zizzy
text: I burned that down too. Great memories.

speaker: zizzy
text: I never had friends who stayed when I lit something. You all stayed.

speaker: zizzy
text: Thanks. Truly. Can I light something now?

speaker: zizzy
text: Wide open space! Perfect for explosions!

speaker: zizzy
text: Look at all the flammable stuff! Not that I'm looking. I'm looking.

speaker: zizzy
text: New room, new ways to set things on fire. I mean, new ways to admire it.

speaker: zizzy
text: Ooh, shiny! Does it go boom? Can it go boom?

speaker: zizzy
text: Loot! Rate: seven out of ten. Would explode again.

speaker: zizzy
text: A secret room! Statistically, there's something flammable in it!

speaker: zizzy
text: Hidden door found! Can I knock on it with a fireball? Gently?

speaker: zizzy
text: That one looks very flammable. Or very not. Let's find out!

speaker: zizzy
text: Big monster! Big boom! It's like we planned it!

speaker: zizzy
text: Town! Everything smells like bread and "please don't set me on fire". Home!

speaker: zizzy
text: Hello, Emberhollow! I promise to be only a little bit explosive.

speaker: vexrath
text: Form 7-B: Application to Exist in a Cave. Filed.

speaker: vexrath
text: Approved. Naturally.

speaker: vexrath
text: My clan forged a decree to exile me. I have written to the Registrar eleven times.

speaker: vexrath
text: The Registrar is, regrettably, a goat.

speaker: vexrath
text: I cannot be certain the decree was forged. I can only be sure.

speaker: vexrath
text: Certainty is not paperwork, but it is close.

speaker: vexrath
text: I have never missed a deadline. I may miss the end of the world.

speaker: vexrath
text: I am preparing a form for that.

speaker: vexrath
text: If I fall, stamp me PROCESSED. And add "with honour." In ink.

speaker: vexrath
text: Pencil is for people who plan to be erased.

speaker: vexrath
text: Room surveyed. No permits on display. Suspicious.

speaker: vexrath
text: Entering an unlicensed chamber. I shall file a report in triplicate.

speaker: vexrath
text: Floor plan acceptable. Ceiling: pending review.

speaker: vexrath
text: Recovered goods. Logged. Stamped. Mine. Ours. Logged.

speaker: vexrath
text: Item received. Chain of custody: us.

speaker: vexrath
text: A concealed passage with no signage. Outrageous. Fascinating.

speaker: vexrath
text: Hidden door located. Form 12-S: Notice of Discovery. Filed.

speaker: vexrath
text: Hostile of exceptional rank. Form 9: Notice of Imminent Violence. Filed.

speaker: vexrath
text: A notable adversary. I shall treat it with the honour it is owed.

speaker: vexrath
text: Emberhollow. Forms are processed here on time. I approve.

speaker: vexrath
text: Municipal lighting inadequate. Morale: acceptable.

speaker: nettle
text: I once fought a hundred rats. Two. One was a ghost rat.

speaker: nettle
text: ...Fine, it was one rat. It bit my boot.

speaker: nettle
text: I've never told a true story to a crowd. They always want the dragon one.

speaker: nettle
text: I'd tell the real one to you, if you'd keep it.

speaker: nettle
text: A mirror and a bard: bad combination. All those versions of me, arguing.

speaker: nettle
text: I came out ahead in every one. Most of them.

speaker: nettle
text: I wrote songs about a hundred heroes. None of them knew me.

speaker: nettle
text: You all know me. It's a strange feeling. A good strange.

speaker: nettle
text: If you ever sing about this, make me taller. Or at least give me better hair.

speaker: nettle
text: And mention I carried the morale. On my back. Like a small mule.

speaker: nettle
text: I once hosted a banquet in a room just like this. Mostly ghosts.

speaker: nettle
text: Fun fact: I designed this style of ceiling. Possibly.

speaker: nettle
text: Hush. I smell a good story, or a bad cheese. Either way.

speaker: nettle
text: I once found a chest like this and gave it to a queen. She never gave it back.

speaker: nettle
text: That is exactly the kind of loot that makes a ballad worthwhile.

speaker: nettle
text: Hidden door! A bard's favourite words: "I knew there was a story here."

speaker: nettle
text: A secret passage. I'll tell this one later, with improvements.

speaker: nettle
text: Big fellow. I once wrestled one of those. It was a tie. I won.

speaker: nettle
text: That one looks like the third act of a tragedy. Let's skip to the comedy.

speaker: nettle
text: Ah, the sweet sound of strangers who owe me a drink.

speaker: nettle
text: Town! I'll be around the tavern, being modest.
